description.narrative:
South West State of Somalia is grappling with a protracted humanitarian crisis driven by decades of conflict, climate change-induced disasters, and weak governance structures. Recurrent droughts, floods, and insecurity have displaced thousands of families, leaving them dependent on humanitarian aid for survival. While numerous humanitarian organizations and aid programs operate in the region,the persistent risks of mismanagement, corruption, and aid diversion threaten to undermine efforts to deliver timely and equitable assistance to those in need. Without effective safeguards, these challenges could further weaken the impact of humanitarian interventions and deepen the suffering of affected communities.
Recognizing the urgent need to safeguard humanitarian resources, the South West State Government has taken a landmark step by enacting the "Safeguarding Humanitarian Assistance Law", which was signed into law by the President of South West State on February 9, 2025. This legislation is designed to protect aid from diversion, enhance transparency, and establish accountability mechanisms to ensure that assistance reaches the most vulnerable populations. The law outlines specific responsibilities for government institutions, humanitarian organizations, and oversight bodies, while also introducing penalties for misconduct and corruption in aid distribution.
The Ministry has developed a well-structured and coordinated implementation to translate the legal provisions into effective action. The plan outlines a four-component strategy focusing on; 1. Public awareness and stakeholder engagement. 2. Strengthening institutional capacity 3. Enhancing the capacity of rule of law institutions to enforce the law. 4. Strength
For the Safeguarding Humanitarian Assistance Law to be effectively enforced, all stakeholders must havea clear understanding of its provisions. Currently, many humanitarian actors, community leaders, and aid beneficiaries lack awareness of their rights and responsibilities under the new framework. This knowledge gap can result in unintentional violations, mismanagement, and reduced public trust in aid distribution processes.Public awareness initiatives will bridge this gap by ensuring that keystakeholders, including community members and relevant stakeholders, are well-informed about the law and their respective roles. Tofacilitate this awareness-building initiative, the ministry will organize public awareness forums in the districts of Burhakaba andDinsoor that target local authorities, religious leaders, traditional elders, youth, and women. More so, the effective implementation of the law requires strong coordination among government institutions, humanitarian agencies and the community members. To facilitate this, regular coordination meetings will be established to provide a platform for MOHADM-Police-prosecutor coordination for aiddiversion-related cases. These meetings will facilitate the sharing of vital information, enhance collaboration, and ensure a unified approach to tackling the challenges posed by aid diversion. ening coordination and compliance mechanisms.
Expected Outcomes • Strengthening coordination among key institutions responsible for investigating and prosecuting aid diversion cases. • Improved case management and evidence-sharing practices. • Enhanced enforcement of penalties under the Safeguarding Humanitarian Assistance Law. • Increased accountability and transparency in humanitarian aid management.

participating-org.narrative:
The MoHADM, acting under the authority of the Galmudug State [Council of Ministers], is responsible for provision and facilitation/coordination of basic support schemes through managing in humanitarian programs and institutions for all vulnerable groups.
Objectives of the ministry:
1. Adequate planning for humanitarian affairs and disaster reduction, preparedness, and management. 2.Advocacy for zero tolerance towards aid misuse. 3. Resource mobilization for humanitarian affairs and disaster management programs in SWS 4. Establishment of regional and district level structures for humanitarian affairs and disaster reduction, preparedness, and management. 5. Well-coordinated and cohesive efforts on humanitarian affairs and disaster prevention andmanagement in SWS by relevant actors. 6. Information and knowledge management on humanitarian affairs and disaster management in SWS. 7. Collection, analysis, management, and dissemination of information on humanitarian affairs and disaster management in SWS.
MOHADM envisions saving lives, alleviating suffering, mitigation disasters, and building resilient communities
MOHADM's mission is to coordinate the formulation and implementation of policies and strategies that enhance management and administration of humanitarian services and disaster and risk management in South West of Somalia
